question: For tax year 2026: (1) the IRS Publication 15-T percentage method for automated payroll, with its annual tables, for an employee who filed a 2020-or-later Form W-4 with no adjustments, for single and for married filing jointly, and for weekly, biweekly and per-shift (daily) pay; (2) what an employer withholds when no W-4 was filed; (3) at year end, who must file a return, the April due date, and how a refund or a balance due arises from withholding versus the annual liability computed from the 2026 brackets and standard deduction already in the research; (4) what happens to an unpaid balance: the failure-to-pay penalty rate and cap, the interest rate rule, notices and when collection begins. Mark each figure with its source and tax year.

title: How much federal income tax an employer withholds from a paycheck, and how the year settles
usableAnswer: The 2026 percentage-method table for single and married filing jointly with the pay-period divisors; the no-W-4 default; the filing threshold and due date; and the penalty and interest rules for a balance due, each cited.
whyItMatters: Every paycheck in the game now records federal income tax withholding as UNKNOWN, so no player or person pays income tax at all. With the method, a paycheck can withhold a real amount, the annual return can compute the real liability from the brackets we already have, and a shortfall becomes an unpaid balance that persists under federal law, as the owner decided.
